q: Which city is an example of an organic pattern, characterized by irregular, winding streets developed without formal planning?
n: Medieval London grew organically, with irregular winding streets and no overall plan. Brasília, New Delhi and Canberra are planned capitals. Source: Kostof, The City Shaped (Organic Patterns).

q: Which Gothic cathedral was the traditional site for the coronation of French kings?
n: Reims Cathedral was the traditional coronation church of the kings of France, from Clovis's baptism through Charles X in 1825. Source: UNESCO World Heritage List – Cathedral of Notre-Dame, Reims; Fletcher, A History of Architecture (French Gothic).

q: Which cathedral became a major pilgrimage site due to its relic, the Sancta Camisia, believed to be the tunic of the Virgin Mary?
n: Chartres Cathedral holds the Sancta Camisia, the tunic believed to have been worn by the Virgin Mary. It made Chartres a major Marian pilgrimage site. Source: UNESCO World Heritage List – Chartres Cathedral; Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture.

q: Which Gothic cathedral was designed to be the tallest, but remains unfinished due to structural collapse?
n: Beauvais Cathedral's choir, at about 48 m the tallest Gothic vault ever built, partly collapsed in 1284. Its tower fell in 1573, and the nave was never built. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (French Gothic); Murray, Beauvais Cathedral.

q: Which of the following cathedrals is especially renowned for its elaborate and preserved rose windows, considered masterpieces of Gothic stained glass?
n: Chartres keeps most of its original 12th–13th-century stained glass, including three great rose windows. They are counted among the masterpieces of Gothic glass. Source: UNESCO World Heritage List – Chartres Cathedral.

q: An architect enters into a design-build contract with a client. Can the same architect be directly and professionally liable for both the design and the construction supervision of the project?
o: Yes, because AoR and AIC can be the same
No, because separate architects shall be hired
No, because a civil engineer is needed
Yes, because it is required under a design-build contract
n: In design-build, one architect may be both the Architect of Record (design) and the Architect-in-Charge of Construction. Both roles are then professionally borne by the same architect. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (Definitions of AoR and AIC); Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 12 (Design-Build Services).

q: Which is an acceptable reason for issuing temporary or special permits to foreign architects and foreign consultants?
n: Temporary or special permits for foreign architects and consultants are justified only where they bring expertise not available locally, with technology transfer to a Filipino counterpart. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38 (Foreign Architects – Special/Temporary Permits).

q: An architect entered into a design-build contract with a private client to design an industrial building with a total project construction cost of ₱24,650,000. The design package includes a sub-consultancy contract between the architect and the allied professionals. What is the recommended professional fee for the administration services?
n: For Design-Build Services by Administration, the architect's fee for administration is 7% of the project construction cost: 7% × ₱24,650,000 = ₱1,725,500. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 12.4 (Design-Build Services).

q: Referring to the previous item, what is the design fee for the project?
n: An industrial building is Group 1. With the engineers sub-contracted (DAEDS), the design fee is 5% of PCC: 5% × ₱24,650,000 = ₱1,232,500. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1 – DAEDS 5%).

q: Referring to the previous items, what is the total billable fee of the architect for the project?
n: Total billable fee = design fee + administration fee = ₱1,232,500 + ₱1,725,500 = ₱2,958,000. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 6.3.1 and Sec. 12.4.

q: The application of anthropometric data to product and environmental design ensures
n: Applying anthropometric data, the measurements of the human body, makes products and spaces fit their users. That gives comfort and functional use. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: An architect is tasked with redesigning a public library to improve user comfort and reduce fatigue during prolonged reading and computer use. She integrates principles focused on optimizing human-device interaction, spatial layout, and posture-supportive furniture design. This design approach is most aligned with which applied science?
n: Ergonomics (human factors) fits workstations, furniture and layouts to the human body and its tasks. It improves comfort and reduces fatigue. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; International Ergonomics Association definition.

q: The idea that one’s own culture is superior to others, often leading to judgment of other cultures using one’s own cultural norms.
n: Ethnocentrism is judging other cultures by the standards of one's own, which is assumed to be superior. Source: Sumner, Folkways (1906); Macionis, Sociology.

q: A society where various cultural groups coexist while maintaining their distinct traditions and practices.
n: Cultural pluralism describes a society where groups coexist while keeping their distinct traditions and identities. Source: Macionis, Sociology (Pluralism, Assimilation, Segregation).

q: A student moves to another country for school and starts using the local language and eating local food, but still practices customs from their home culture and celebrates traditional holidays. This process is best described as
n: Acculturation is adopting elements of a new culture, such as its language and food, while keeping one's own customs. Assimilation would mean giving up the home culture. Source: Berry, Acculturation Strategies; Macionis, Sociology.

q: What is the minimum rear setback of a housing unit intended for low-income families?
n: Under BP 220, the minimum yards for economic and socialized housing units are 1.5 m front, 1.5 m side and 2.0 m rear. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR (2008), Design Standards – Setbacks/Yards.

q: Which of the following is an allowed use of an alley?
n: An alley (2.0 m) is for pedestrians and emergency passage only, connecting two streets. It cannot be used as a property access, a minor road or for parking. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Design Standards – Circulation.

q: What is the minimum frontage of a single-attached housing unit in an economic subdivision project?
n: BP 220 sets the minimum lot frontage of single-attached and duplex units at 6.0 m for both economic and socialized housing. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Table – Minimum Lot Frontage.

q: Who is the architect of the Church of the Risen Lord at the University of the Philippines, Diliman?
n: Cesar Concio designed the Church of the Risen Lord at UP Diliman (1955–56), with its folded-plate concrete roof. Source: University of the Philippines Diliman heritage records; CCP Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Architecture).

q: Which architect designed the towering Art Deco monument located at the center of a major elliptical road in Quezon City, built to honor a former Philippine president and featuring three vertical pylons representing Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao?
n: Federico Ilustre designed the Quezon Memorial Shrine at the Quezon Memorial Circle. Its three pylons represent Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao, and they are topped by mourning angels. Source: National Historical Commission of the Philippines, Quezon Memorial Shrine marker.

q: The Ramon Magsaysay Center, one of the earliest high-rise structures in Manila, was designed by
n: Alfredo J. Luz designed the Ramon Magsaysay Center on Roxas Boulevard (1967), one of Manila's early high-rises. Source: CCP Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Architecture – Alfredo J. Luz).

q: Which of the following Filipino architects is best known for using the Art Deco style in many of his works?
n: Pablo Antonio, National Artist for Architecture, is best known for Art Deco works such as the Far Eastern University buildings and the Manila Polo Club. Source: NCCA, Order of National Artists – Pablo S. Antonio.

q: Which of the following describes the National Press Club building by Angel Nakpil?
n: Angel Nakpil's National Press Club building in Intramuros (1955) is a post-war modernist design. Source: CCP Encyclopedia of Philippine Art (Architecture – Angel Nakpil).

q: What is the maximum allowable height for beds in accessible guest rooms?
n: Beds in accessible guest rooms should have a top surface no higher than about 450–500 mm. That allows level transfer from a wheelchair seat. Source: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR (Accessible Guest Rooms); ADA Standards, Sec. 806.

q: What is an exit or a means of going out of a building?
n: Egress is the means of going out of a building, or the exit path. Ingress is the means of entering. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Definitions (Means of Egress); NFPA 101.

q: What is the maximum allowable angle of inclination for an escalator?
n: Escalators are normally inclined at no more than 30°. A slightly steeper 35° is allowed only for short rises at low speed. Source: ASME A17.1 / EN 115-1 (Escalators – Angle of Inclination).

q: Which of the following is a distinct feature of Greek temple architecture, known for its use of post-and-lintel construction and proportionally balanced forms?
n: Greek temples are trabeated (post and lintel): fluted columns carry an entablature of architrave, frieze and cornice in harmonic proportions. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Greek); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which innovative Roman architectural feature allowed for the creation of large interior spaces without interior supports, transforming the scale of public buildings?
n: Roman concrete barrel and groin vaults spanned large interiors without intermediate supports, as in the baths and basilicas. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Roman); MacDonald, The Architecture of the Roman Empire.

q: What is the most distinguishing structural innovation in Byzantine church architecture, allowing the transition from a square base to a circular dome?
n: Pendentives are curved spherical triangles that carry a circular dome over a square bay. They are the defining Byzantine innovation, as at Hagia Sophia. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Byzantine); Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which of the following was a dominant plan in Early Christian basilicas, characterized by a long nave, side aisles, and an apse at one end?
n: The Early Christian basilica was a longitudinal rectangular plan: a tall nave flanked by side aisles and ending in an apse, as at Old St. Peter's. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Early Christian); Krautheimer, Early Christian and Byzantine Architecture.

q: Which type of ornamentation, often depicting religious figures surrounded by gold backgrounds, became a signature feature of Byzantine interiors?
n: Byzantine interiors were covered with tesserae mosaics of glass and gold tiles. Holy figures were set against shimmering gold grounds, as at Ravenna and Hagia Sophia. Source: Krautheimer, Early Christian and Byzantine Architecture; Fletcher, A History of Architecture.

q: Who shall review the building permit application for green buildings?
n: Compliance with the Philippine Green Building Code is reviewed by the Office of the Building Official as part of the building permit application. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Administration and Enforcement; PD 1096 (Building Official).

q: For energy efficiency, air tightness can be maximized by increasing attention to
n: Airtightness depends on careful construction details: continuous air barriers and sealed joints, penetrations and junctions between envelope elements. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Building Envelope; ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals (Air Leakage).

q: What can be added to glazed windows to reduce the SHGC of the window?
n: External shading devices (sunbreakers) block direct sun before it reaches the glass. That lowers the effective solar heat gain coefficient of the window more than interior curtains do. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting, Ch. 9 (Shading); Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: Steel is ____ recyclable.
n: Steel can be recycled indefinitely (100%) without losing its properties. Source: World Steel Association, Steel – the Permanent Material; Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Materials.

q: A student is seated in a naturally ventilated classroom during the afternoon. Although the air temperature is moderate, she feels warm due to the surrounding sunlit walls and ceiling. Which environmental factor is most likely affecting her thermal comfort?
n: Mean radiant temperature is the average temperature of the surrounding surfaces. Hot sunlit walls and ceilings raise it, so occupants feel warm even when the air temperature is moderate. Source: ASHRAE Standard 55 (Thermal Environmental Conditions); Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: Which of the following conditions is most likely to promote mold growth in a tropical indoor environment?
o: high air velocity and low humidity
low relative humidity and direct sunlight
high relative humidity and poor ventilation
n: Mold grows where relative humidity stays high (above about 60–70%) and air stagnates, which is common in poorly ventilated tropical interiors. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals (Moisture Management); US EPA, Mold Guide.

q: This is the measure of heat transfer through a material, often used in evaluating wall and roof assemblies in hot climates.
n: The U-value (thermal transmittance, W/m²·K) measures the rate of heat transfer through an assembly. Lower is better. R-value is its reciprocal resistance. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – Fundamentals, Ch. 26; Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: Which of the following properties measures a material’s ability to reflect solar radiation and reduce surface heat buildup?
o: SRI 168.In traditional Bahay na Bato architecture, ventanillas are small operable openings typically located:
n: The Solar Reflectance Index (SRI) combines solar reflectance and thermal emittance. It shows how well a surface stays cool in the sun. Source: ASTM E1980 (Solar Reflectance Index); Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: In traditional bahay na bato architecture, ventanillas are small operable openings typically located
o: at the center of the wall for structural balance
near the ceiling to release rising warm air
between the floor and the window sill to allow airflow while maintaining privacy
n: Ventanillas are small openings with sliding panels or balusters between the floor and the window sill of the bahay na bato. They let in air while preserving privacy. Source: Perez, Encarnacion & Dacanay, Folk Architecture; Zialcita & Tinio, Philippine Ancestral Houses.
